chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The man must not swear an oath except based upon his knowledge.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a valid oath in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores that the validity of an oath (yamin) is contingent upon the swearer's actual knowledge, preventing perjury and ensuring legal integrity. It serves as a foundational principle for distinguishing between binding oaths and those that are merely casual, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on precision in speech and accountability before God.
